correctness.rationale: Orthogonal graph spectral decomposition has eigenvalues n, m and m+n; exact integration gives the cross factor rho=4 lambda mu/(lambda+mu)^2. Expanding fourth powers yields the displayed exact deficit. With at most two vertices in each part the cubic terms cancel and the residual squares are nonnegative; single-eigenvalue inputs attain 1/2. A three-site contrast and delta=1/4 give the explicit strictly negative rational deficit on any larger part. The argument is valid for all positive part sizes and arbitrary Hilbert-space values. Standalone exact-fraction tests replayed for ordered pairs through 20.

value.rationale: The sharp L2-to-L4 benchmark is a natural nontrivial quantitative question for heat g-functions. The claim settles it on every K_mn, distinguishes C4 (contractive) from K1,3 (amplifying), provides a universal exact Hilbert-space deficit with equality and simple witnesses for all larger parts. This is an infinite-family structural boundary, not an arbitrary finite enumeration or small numerical refinement. It does not attempt the unknown superbenchmark sharp norm.
